title: Pay a Contractor via Unified Identity
description: Pay freelance contractors using one unified profile shared across contacts, payroll, communication, and expense tracking.
prerequisites: You can manage contact records and run payroll.
You have permission to assign contact folders and payroll visibility.
steps: Create or open the contractor's record in Contact Directory and avoid creating separate duplicate profiles in other systems.
Assign the contact to the Contractors folder to classify them for payroll and operational workflows.
Open Run Payroll and verify the contractor appears automatically from the same unified identity.
Log approved contractor time and applicable expenses against this profile.
Generate and process contractor payment from payroll, keeping all references tied to the unified identity.
Confirm the same identity remains usable for communication, payment history, and operational reporting.
validations: Contractor appears in payroll from the same contact identity.
Time, expense, and payment records reference one profile ID.
No duplicate contractor profiles exist across CRM and payroll areas.
commonErrors: Separate contractor records are created in CRM and payroll.
Contractor not visible in Run Payroll after profile setup.
Expenses logged under a different identity than payment record.
recovery: Merge duplicate contractor profiles and preserve the canonical unified identity.
Reclassify contractor folder assignment and refresh payroll listing.
Relink misfiled time/expense entries to the canonical contractor record.

faq.question: Should contractors live in HR or CRM?
faq.answer: Use one unified contact identity that serves both operational communication and payroll workflows.

faq.question: Can I track communication and payments under one profile?
faq.answer: Yes. Unified Identity keeps email, time, expenses, and payments tethered to the same entity.
